I am already thinking about this year the same way I always do. My land is only 8 mu, and just two of us are working, so I cannot gamble too much. Wheat-maize is what our place knows best. If I leave wheat, I lose one season of grain, and if I delay maize after wheat harvest, that also hurts. I will mostly do what has worked on my fields before, with only small adjustments. Wheat needs steady fertilizer and a few waterings if the spring is dry. Maize must go in fast after wheat harvest, so I will keep land preparation simple and not do anything fancy. I watch what the good households nearby do, and usually if they irrigate wheat 3 times and maize once or twice, I do about the same. Fertilizer is expensive, so I will not push too high, but I also do not want the crop to look weak and lose yield for saving a little money.

For wheat, I will use improved local seed like most people here, sow in early October, put most fertilizer as base, then add a topdress around jointing if the leaves are pale. Since I have a well, I will irrigate when it matters most, but not too many times because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away, within a few days, because if I wait the stand will be poor and yield drops. Maize I usually fertilize a bit less than wheat, mostly one base dose and one later feeding. If weeds come, I spray once. If insects are light, I do not spray much. This way I keep the crop safe, keep cash in hand, and do not make too many risky changes at my age.
